 UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following  O R D E R The Special Leave Petitions will remain pending.
The interim orders passed in the present Special Leave Petitions will remain in force.

It will naturally be open for the Authorities under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (for the sake of convenience hereinafter referred to as the Act) to take such action as may be warranted in law from time to time.
The trial against the petitioners under the provisions of the Act, which are stated to be presently pending, to be expedited and completed within an outer limit of six months from today.
The matters be listed after the trails against the petitioners in the present Special Leave Petitions are concluded.

Needless to say, the trial Court will conduct the trial and conclude the same without, in any manner, being influenced by any finding, observation or view that has been recorded by the High Court in the Orders dated 30th January, 2014, 13th February, 2014 and 24th March, 2014 in PIL No.01 of 2012.

It has been brought to our notice by the learned counsel appearing for the respondent No.7 (PIL Petitioner) that the implementation of the provisions of the Act in the State of Jammu & Kashmir has been somewhat tardy.
If the Act is in force in the State, there must be strict implementation thereof and the State Government must ensure the same.

When the matters come up on the next date, the State of Jammu & Kashmir will file a report before this Court with regard to the state of Khyber Agro Farms Pvt Ltd vs The State Of Jammu And Kashmir on 4 February, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44868499/
